outline.description: Introduce the problem setting: the rise of large foundation models, the computational cost of pretraining, and the need for parameter-efficient finetuning (PEFT). Present an overview of existing PEFT strategies, motivate orthogonal finetuning (OFT), and summarize the contributions and high-level ideas of the BOFT (Orthogonal Butterfly Finetuning) paper.
sections: Large-scale foundation models and fine-tuning challenges
Three families of PEFT: full finetuning, adapters, prompt tuning
Reparameterization approaches: LoRA and related methods
Motivation for orthogonality: preserving pretraining structure
Limitations of existing OFT and the parameter-efficiency problem
High-level idea of BOFT and a roadmap of the textbook

outline.description: Provide the mathematical background necessary for the rest of the book. Review linear algebra concepts (matrices, orthogonality, SVD), matrix groups, sparse matrices, block structures, and basic optimization notions used in finetuning. Also introduce graph representations of matrix sparsity and basic notions from signal processing (FFT) that will be used later.
sections: Vectors, matrices, inner products and norms
Orthogonal matrices and orthonormal bases
Skew-symmetric matrices and Cayley transform
Singular value decomposition and spectral norm
Matrix sparsity patterns, block matrices and low-rank factorizations
Matrix factorization vs additive updates (multiplicative vs additive reparameterization)
Graph representations of matrices: adjacency and information flow
Brief overview of FFT and the Cooley–Tukey algorithm (intuition)

outline.description: A deeper review of the PEFT landscape, with technical descriptions and strengths/weaknesses of representative methods, including LoRA, adapters, prompt tuning, BitFit, and prior orthogonal finetuning work. This chapter sets the baseline context to compare BOFT against.
sections: Full finetuning: benefits and pitfalls
Adapter modules: architecture, parameter count, use cases
Prompt tuning and prefix tuning: mechanism and limitations
LoRA: low-rank updates, mathematical formulation and practicalities
Reparameterization-based PEFT methods beyond LoRA
Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT): original formulation and empirical findings
Comparative summary: parameter budgets, inference cost, and generalization

outline.description: Formalize Orthogonal Finetuning: how OFT reparameterizes pretrained weights multiplicatively using orthogonal matrices, Cayley parameterization to enforce orthogonality, initialization, block-diagonal OFT for efficiency, and the intuition behind angle preservation and generalization.
sections: OFT formal definition: multiplicative reparameterization
Preserving pairwise neuron angles: why orthogonality?
Cayley transform for orthogonal parameterization: derivation and properties
Zero/identity initialization and its role in finetuning
Block-diagonal OFT: motivation, parameter savings, and limitations
Practical considerations: optimization, stability and empirical behavior
Where OFT works well and where it struggles

outline.chapter_title: 5. An Information Transmission View of Matrix Factorization
outline.description: Introduce the novel perspective from the paper: viewing factorizing a dense matrix as an information transmission problem on a layered grid graph. Formalize the unrolled graph representation, define desiderata (dense connectivity, minimum free edges), and analyze how different sparsity patterns map to connectivity patterns.
sections: Motivation for graphical interpretation of matrix multiplication
Unrolling matrix products into a d × (m+1) grid graph
Edges, nodes, and interpretation of nonzero entries
Desiderata: dense connectivity and minimum free edges under orthogonality
Orthogonality constraints as structural constraints on edges
Examples: block-diagonal factorization and its graph
Using the information transmission view to search for efficient topologies

outline.chapter_title: 6. Butterfly Structures and the Cooley–Tukey Algorithm
outline.description: Explain butterfly graphs and matrices, their origin in FFT, recursive structure, and why they are efficient for information mixing. Define butterfly factors and butterfly matrices formally, and discuss block/batched (block-butterfly) generalizations used in BOFT.
sections: The Cooley–Tukey FFT: recursive divide-and-conquer and the butterfly diagram
Definition of a butterfly factor and butterfly component
Recursive construction of a full butterfly matrix
Properties: sparsity, depth (O(log d)), and O(d log d) nonzeros
Block butterfly matrices: definition and motivation (handling channels/blocks)
Examples of transforms expressible via butterfly factorization (DFT, Hadamard)
Butterfly graphs as an efficient network topology for information transmission

outline.description: Present the BOFT method in detail: how BOFT composes dense orthogonal matrices from a product of sparse orthogonal butterfly components, parameter counts BOFT(m, b), special cases connecting BOFT and OFT, and practical design choices.
sections: BOFT reparameterization: R(m, b) = product of orthogonal butterfly components
Ensuring orthogonality of each component via Cayley parameterization or block rotations
Block size b and number of stages m: trade-offs and parameter count formula
Recovering OFT as special cases (m = 1, b = d and m = 1 general block-diagonal)
Dense orthogonal matrices with O(d log d) parameters when m = log d and b = 2
Identity initialization for BOFT and rationale
Practical instantiation: choices of permutations, block types and implementation notes

outline.chapter_title: 8. Training BOFT: Regularization, Dropout and Optimization
outline.description: Discuss training details and regularization strategies specific to BOFT. Explain multiplicative dropout adapted to multiplicative updates, optimization strategies, computational and memory costs, and tips to accelerate training and maintain stability.
sections: Optimization setup: learning rates, optimizers, and stability considerations
Multiplicative Dropout: concept, implementation, and hyperparameters
Why conventional dropout doesn't apply and the block-drop scheme
Initialization strategies and zero/identity start for safe finetuning
Computational complexity: per-step cost and trade-offs vs OFT/LoRA
Memory considerations and ways to fuse matrices post-training
Practical heuristics: when to use larger b vs larger m

outline.chapter_title: 9. Theoretical Analysis: Expressivity, Spectra and Bias
outline.description: Present the theoretical insights from the paper: expressivity claims (Theorem on BOFT expressivity), spectral properties (why orthogonality preserves spectral norm), bilinear similarity interpretation, and discussion of inductive biases introduced by butterfly structures.
sections: Expressivity of BOFT: statement and intuition of the main theorem
Kaleidoscope hierarchy and how products of butterfly matrices approach full orthogonal group
Proof sketch and key lemmas (high-level, accessible)
Spectral properties: why BOFT preserves singular values and implications
BOFT as learning bilinear similarity / metric learning interpretation
Inductive bias induced by structured factorization: benefits and risks
When more expressivity can harm generalization: trade-offs explained

outline.chapter_title: 10. Experimental Design: Tasks, Models and Baselines
outline.description: Lay out the experiments used to validate BOFT: datasets, downstream tasks (vision classification, language tasks, text-to-image diffusion), model families (ViTs, LLMs, diffusion models), baseline methods (LoRA, OFT, adapters), and metrics. Include details needed for reproducibility and fair comparison.
sections: Overview of downstream tasks and why they were chosen
Model families: vision transformers, language models, diffusion-based generative models
Dataset details for vision, language and generation tasks
Baselines and competing PEFT methods to compare against
Evaluation metrics and experimental protocol
Hyperparameter sweep and budgets: controlling for parameter counts
Reproducibility considerations and computational resource reporting

outline.description: Present and interpret empirical findings: main results showing BOFT's performance and parameter-efficiency, ablations on block size and stage count, convergence and stability plots, interpolation/visualization of learned weights, and qualitative examples for generative tasks.
sections: Main quantitative results across tasks and model families
Parameter-efficiency plots: performance vs number of trainable parameters
Ablation: effect of m (number of butterfly stages) and b (block size)
Comparisons with LoRA and original OFT: accuracy, stability and generalization
Convergence behavior and training stability analysis
Visualization: weight interpolation and matrix approximation diagnostics
Qualitative examples: text-to-image generations and failure cases
Discussion: what the experiments reveal about inductive bias and practical use

outline.description: Hands-on guidance for implementing BOFT in modern ML toolkits. Provide pseudo-code, describe modular implementation patterns (layers, modules), techniques to reduce runtime overhead, and step-by-step instructions to apply BOFT to a pretrained model and fuse weights for deployment.
sections: Pseudo-code for BOFT forward and backward passes
Implementing Cayley parameterization for block components (code snippets)
Integrating BOFT into PyTorch / TensorFlow model layers
Efficient batched multiplication of sparse factors and permutation handling
Optimizations: grouping blocks, custom CUDA kernels, and lazy fusion
Post-training fusion: multiplying R into pretrained weights for inference
Suggested hyperparameter defaults for common model families
Common pitfalls and debugging checklist

outline.chapter_title: 13. Extensions, Limitations and Future Research Directions
outline.description: Analyze limitations of BOFT (training overhead, non-power-of-two dims, unknown optimal topologies) and propose avenues for future work: alternative network topologies, hybrid methods combining low-rank and butterfly factorizations, automated architecture search over factorization, and broader applications.
sections: Limitations highlighted in the paper: training runtime and overhead
Handling non-power-of-two dimensions and irregular block sizes
Is butterfly optimal? Other network topologies from communication theory
Combining BOFT with LoRA or adapters: hybrid PEFT strategies
Automatic search for factorization parameters (m, b) per layer
Theoretical open problems: expressivity vs generalization trade-offs
Potential applications beyond supervised finetuning (compression, pruning)
Experimental directions: larger models, multi-task finetuning, continual learning

outline.description: Provide pedagogical exercises and project prompts to let students deepen their understanding. Exercises range from mathematical proofs, small-scale implementations, experiments to reproduce paper results, and open-ended research projects.
sections: Mathematical exercises (e.g., properties of Cayley transform, small proofs)

Project: design an alternative factorization topology and test it
